text: Temporary Authenticated DSH Web 为 DSH Web GUI 提供当前进程的鉴权地址，并支持按会话启动独立的临时 Web 实例。插件注册 gui_auth_url 工具、/dsh-web 命令和实例管理工具，可获取当前 GUI 地址、启动或重启临时实例、查询状态并停止实例。适合浏览器自动化访问 GUI，或在隔离的临时配置中试用插件。临时实例默认可继承当前 DeepSeek API key。

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web returns the current GUI address and manages session-specific temporary DSH Web instances. Use its command or agent tools to start, restart, inspect, and stop instances for browser automation or plugin trials. The instance can inherit the current DeepSeek API key.
让浏览器自动化拿到当前 DSH Web 界面的可用登录地址。
我想开一个独立的临时 DSH Web 环境来试插件。
能不能从 agent 工具启动并重启一个会话专属的 Web 实例？
Temporary Authenticated DSH Web 的功能「获取 GUI 地址」：调用 gui_auth_url，返回当前 Web GUI 的鉴权地址供浏览器打开。
Temporary Authenticated DSH Web 的功能「临时实例管理」：用 /dsh-web 或 agent 工具启动、重启、查询和停止会话专属的 DSH Web 实例。
Temporary Authenticated DSH Web 默认会把当前进程解析到的 DEEPSEEK_API_KEY 传给临时实例进程；可用 shareApiKey: false 关闭。

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · dsh-gui-auth-url：English | [中文](README-zh.md) | [Español](README-es.md) | [Português](README-pt.md) | [हिन्दी](README-hi.md)

Expose the running DeepSeek Harness Web GUI's **authenticated URL** as an agent tool, so browser automation and scripts can open the GUI instead of hitting `401 dsh web authentication required`.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · dsh-gui-auth-url：It also ships **temporary authenticated DSH Web**: an agent (`dsh_web_start` / `dsh_web_restart` / `dsh_web_stop` / `dsh_web_status` tools) or a person (`/dsh-web` command — start when absent, restart in place when running) can get a per-session instance with its own throwaway `DSH_HOME` and port, to exercise new plugins, surfaces, or profiles without touching the live session — one per session, sessions never disturb each other, and an instance only ever exists as a tracked background job bound to a session.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · The problem：`dsh --profile web` mints a random launch token per process and prints it once:

```text
dsh web: http://127.0.0.1:3080/?token=...
```

`GET /?token=...` verifies the token, sets a signed cookie bound to host:port, and redirects to `/`. Opening the bare address returns:

```text
401 dsh web authentication required; reopen the URL printed by dsh web.
```

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · The problem：The Desktop edition starts its own Host process on a random port and never prints that line, so any external browser or automation tool opening `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` always gets 401. There is no `--no-browser-auth` switch today.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · How it works：The plugin runs inside the Host process and asks the official public API `connection.authenticatedUrl(baseUrl)` — the same call `dsh web` uses to build the URL it prints — then returns the result as a tool result.

It never reads the cookie-signing secret in `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml` and never mints a cookie itself, so the URL is a genuine first-party session bound to this process.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · How it works：Base URL resolution prefers `webApp.getAdvertisedUrl()` (respects `--public-url` and mounts), then `webServer.getOrigin()`, then protocol plus loopback port. Every call re-reads the live value, so random Desktop ports and restarted tokens need no cache. The token is attached only when that base is absolute `http` or `https`, has no username or password, and — unless the plugin config sets `allowPublic: true` — names a loopback host (`127.0.0.0/8`, `localhost`, or `::1`). The returned URL must be that same origin and carry exactly one `token`. An unacceptable base is refused before `authenticatedUrl` is called, and the error text never includes the URL.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` writes the bundle into the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` automatically. Restart DeepSeek Harness and the tool appears.

Local checkout instead:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url.git
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-gui-auth-url
```

The package is published on npm as `dsh-gui-auth-url`. GitHub is the source repository.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Install：Upgrading from the old name `dsh-gui-session` (0.1.x): the package name, Cordis row id and tool name all changed, so reinstall once:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <name> remove dsh-gui-session
dsh plugin --profile <name> add github:NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url
```

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Usage：The plugin registers one read-only agent tool, `gui_auth_url`, four instance tools — `dsh_web_start`, `dsh_web_restart`, `dsh_web_stop`, `dsh_web_status` — and one human command, `/dsh-web` (the old `/web-gui` spelling stays executable as an alias). The read-only tool returns:

```json
{
  "url": "http://127.0.0.1:3080/?token=...",
  "origin": "http://127.0.0.1:3080",
  "protocol": "http:",

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Usage：The model sees the `url` text; the other fields are available to programmatic callers. Hand the URL to `navigate_page`, `curl`, or any HTTP client to enter the GUI.

Typical use: while debugging DeepSeek Harness itself, let the agent open the live GUI with chrome-devtools-mcp and verify layout, interaction and RPC for real instead of guessing from code.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Usage：`/dsh-web` is the human half: type it in the GUI input box and the plugin decides for you — with no instance for this session it spawns a **separate** `dsh web` host with its own temporary `DSH_HOME` and an OS-assigned port; with one already running it restarts it in place, keeping the temporary home and anything installed into it, and reusing the same port so an open tab keeps working (only the launch token changes). Either way it opens the new URL in the system default browser. Nothing is shared with the desktop edition's live session, so the browser GUI is a disposable, isolated place to work. Each session owns its own host, so Session A's instance is never reused or stopped by Session B. An instance only ever exists while bound to a session: a call with no session id, or a job registry that refuses the ownership binding, fails instead of leaving an unowned host. The instance is a tracked session job whose registry owner is the **invoking session id**, so the desktop session keeps showing "running" in its header control and you can stop it there; archiving that session while it runs lists it as live activity in the archive confirmat

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Usage：- `install` (string[]): package specs to install into the temporary `DSH_HOME` with `dsh plugin --profile web add` before the host boots. This is how a local or published plugin gets tried inside a throwaway instance. At most 16 specs per call, and a spec may not start with `-` (that would be a package-manager flag). **Cost:** pnpm runs those packages' lifecycle scripts as your user, so only name packages you are willing to run; failure is terminal — the error carries the tail of the install output (capped at 4,000 characters), no host is left running, and a fresh start also deletes the temporary home while an in-place restart leaves the preserved home for the startup sweep. Install is allowed by default; set `allowInstall: false` in the profile patch to reject every request that carries `install`.
- `host` (string): the bind address. It must be a concrete IPv4 or IPv6 literal — `0.0.0.0`, `::` and `*` are refused, because a wildcard would publish the instance on every interface. Accepted only when the plugin config is exactly `allowPublic: true`.
- `public_url` (string): the advertised root URL; absolute `http` or `https`, no username

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Usage：Turning `allowPublic` on is the one setting that widens the blast radius: the instance then answers beyond loopback, and the token is all that stands between that network and a signed-in session. Leave it unset on a loopback desktop profile.

**Complete loop: a local plugin, tried in a throwaway instance.** `install` on `dsh_web_restart` is what turns "install, restart to load it, verify, tear down" into one clean cycle:

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Usage：```text
1. dsh_web_start()
   -> { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:49312/?token=...", "jobId": "job-..." }

2. dsh_web_restart({ "install": ["D:/tools/dsh-plugins/dsh-gui-auth-url"] })

For a fresh instance, `dsh_web_start({ "install": [...] })` collapses steps 1 and 2 into one call. Either way everything lands in `%TEMP%/dsh-web-gui-*`, and a restart keeps that home so the install survives.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Usage：Agents get five entries, and they are not interchangeable: `gui_auth_url` returns this process's own address (the GUI the person is looking at, read-only and side-effect free); `dsh_web_start` starts this session's isolated host and returns its `url`, `jobId` and `reused` **without opening a browser** — a bare call reuses the running instance, while a call carrying `install` or an exposure argument restarts it in place, because that is a request for a differently configured host; `dsh_web_restart` replaces that host in place, keeps the temporary home, inherits every exposure option it is not given, and re-runs the install only when the call names specs again; `dsh_web_stop` stops it, deletes the temporary home, and returns `{ stopped }` — `stopped: false` when there was nothing to stop, which is not an error; `dsh_web_status` reports the session's instance without changing anything — `running`, `runningCount`, `maxInstances`, and while an instance is recorded also `startedAt`, `home`, `port`, `sharedKey`, `install`, `exposed` and `jobStatus`, plus `url` and `jobId` while it is running. All five stop paths — roster, `job_kill`, `dsh_web

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Usage：The browser half also relabels the command in Chinese and adds an icon where the client exposes them; that patch degrades to a no-op if a future client supports label/icon natively.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Security：- The returned URL contains **this process's launch token**. It is a credential equivalent to a signed-in session and only works while the Host process is alive.
- Do not write it to logs, commit it, or paste it into chats. Regenerate by calling the tool again; a restart invalidates it.
- A successful call still places the token in the session transcript and in later model requests. "Do not write it to logs" does not stop the host from storing the tool result. That is a wider audience than the one line `dsh web` prints in a terminal.
- The plugin does not read `.credentials.yaml` and does not mint cookies.
- Non-loopback URLs (`--public-url`, a LAN address, or `0.0.0.0`) are refused unless the plugin config is exactly `allowPublic: true`. That flag trusts the advertised host.
- An isolated instance is a real `dsh web` child process. With `shareApiKey: true` (the default) it receives this process's `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` through its environment: not written to the temporary home and not printed, but readable by any process running as the same user, and every turn inside it bills the same account. `shareApiKey: false` opts out.
- `install

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Compatibility：Display metadata (`locale/*.json` plus the exported `./icon`) makes the Plugins page and Settings show a proper title, description and artwork instead of the raw package id. The plugin does not require a build step: it ships plain ESM JavaScript.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Troubleshooting：**Installation rejected because of a version mismatch.** DSH checks `engines.dsh` (or dsh peer ranges) at install time. If your host is outside the declared range, grant the exact-version exemption, reinstall, and revoke it once a compatible release exists:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> version-exemptions
dsh plugin --profile <profile> allow-version dsh-gui-auth-url@0.2.1 --dsh-version <runtime> --accept-risk
dsh plugin --profile <profile> revoke-version dsh-gui-auth-url@0.2.1
```

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Troubleshooting：**`EPERM: rename ... node_modules\dsh-gui-auth-url_tmp_*` on Windows.** Stop the DSH process using that profile, delete the stale `node_modules\dsh-gui-auth-url` directory, and retry. A running process locks the directory.

**"This profile serves no Web GUI".** The plugin only returns a URL when the profile mounts `webApp` or `webServer` plus `connection`. Headless-style profiles have no GUI to open.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Troubleshooting：**"refusing to attach the launch token to a non-loopback host".** The advertised URL is not loopback. The token is not returned. To allow that host, set this entry in the profile patch. A later patch replaces the whole `config` object, so keep any other keys you need in that same object:

```yaml
- id: gui-auth-url
  config:
    allowPublic: true
```

Leave `allowPublic` unset on a Desktop loopback profile. The flag trusts whatever `webApp.getAdvertisedUrl()` returns.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Troubleshooting：**`dsh_web_start` refuses `install`.** Either the profile config is `allowInstall: false`, or a spec contains a character outside `[A-Za-z0-9@._~:/\\+=%-]` (a space, a quote, `&|<>^`). Fix the spec, or re-enable installs in the profile patch if you meant to use them.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Troubleshooting：**An install fails and no instance appears.** That is the intended behaviour: the temporary home is deleted and the error carries the tail of the install output. Read that tail — usually it is a version mismatch (`engines.dsh`, see the exemption flow above) or a registry/network failure. Nothing is left half-installed to clean up.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Troubleshooting：**`dsh_web_start` refuses `host`, `public_url`, `tls_cert`, `tls_key` or `trusted_host`.** Exposure arguments are refused unless the config is exactly `allowPublic: true`. A wildcard (`0.0.0.0`, `::`, `*`) is refused even then — pass a concrete address and keep any reverse proxy or tunnel outside the plugin.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Troubleshooting：**A restart invalidated the URL.** Only the port is reused, and only when it is free; the launch token changes on every start and restart, so older links answer 401. Call `dsh_web_status` for the current `url`.

**`dsh_web_stop` reports nothing was stopped.** This session had no instance by then — already stopped, killed from the task roster, or ended with `job_kill`. `dsh_web_status` confirms before you assume it failed.

node --test test/*.test.js          # unit + manifest compliance tests
node --check src/index.js && node --check src/auth-url.js && node --check src/api-key.js && node --check src/command.js && node --check src/isolated-tool.js && node --check src/isolated-web.js && node --check client.js
npm run check:pack                  # verifies the published tarball contents
```

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Development：```text
src/auth-url.js      pure helpers: base URL resolution + Host session call (unit-tested)
src/api-key.js       DeepSeek API key resolution for the isolated host
src/command.js       /dsh-web command: start/auto-restart and browser opening
src/isolated-web.js  per-session instance manager (spawn, restart, stop, sweep)

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Development：The plugin registers one read-only tool, four instance tools and one human command; `ctx.tools.register` disposers belong to Cordis, so unloading or hot-reloading the plugin removes them cleanly.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Development：Pushing a `v*` tag runs `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, which publishes to npm through **trusted publishing (OIDC)**: the workflow carries no npm token and needs no repository secret. The package must already have a trusted publisher registered for this repository and workflow file — see [Releasing](#releasing). Publishing from a local machine stays valid.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Releasing：Releases take one command: `npm run release -- patch|minor|major` (add `--dry-run` to preview without changing anything). It runs the full validation chain (tests, syntax, pack) first and aborts untouched when a check fails; then it bumps the version, commits, tags and pushes. The tag triggers `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, which publishes to npm through **trusted publishing (OIDC)** — no npm token and no repository secret are involved.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Releasing：Register the trusted publisher once. On npmjs.com → Packages → `dsh-gui-auth-url` → Settings → Trusted publishing → GitHub Actions:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Organization or user | `NingYuanLee` |
| Repository | `dsh-gui-auth-url` |
| Workflow filename | `publish.yml` (file name only, extension included, case must match exactly) |
| Environment name | leave empty |

The same entry can be created from the CLI (npm ≥ 11.15.0, account 2FA enabled, package already on the registry):

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Releasing：```bash
npm trust github dsh-gui-auth-url --file publish.yml --repo NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url --allow-publish
```

`--allow-publish` lets this workflow run `npm publish`; `npm stage publish` is always allowed. Trusted publishing needs npm CLI ≥ 11.5.1 and Node ≥ 22.14.0 — the publish workflow runs on Node 24 (npm 11.16), which satisfies both — and provenance is attached automatically.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Releasing：To publish from a local machine instead, use the official flow: `npm login --auth-type=web` gives a two-hour session token, and the publish itself needs a 2FA one-time code:

```bash
npm login --auth-type=web
npm publish --access public --tag latest --otp <code>
```

If your host is outside the declared range, grant the exact-version exemption, reinstall, and revoke it once a compatible release exists:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> version-exemptions
dsh plugin --profile <profile> allow-version dsh-gui-auth-url@0.2.1 --dsh-version <runtime> --accept-risk

```

**"This profile serves no Web GUI".** The plugin only returns a URL when the profile mounts `webApp` or `webServer` plus `connection`. Headless-style profiles have no GUI to open.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Troubleshooting：**"refusing to attach the launch token to a non-loopback host".** The advertised URL is not loopback. The token is not returned. To allow that host, set this entry in the profile patch. A later patch replaces the whole `config` object, so keep any other keys you need in that same object:

```

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Troubleshooting：**`dsh_web_start` refuses `install`.** Either the profile config is `allowInstall: false`, or a spec contains a character outside `[A-Za-z0-9@._~:/\\+=%-]` (a space, a quote, `&|<>^`). Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Troubleshooting：**An install fails and no instance appears.** That is the intended behaviour: the temporary home is deleted and the error carries the tail of the install output. Read that tail — usually it is a version mismatch (`engines.dsh`, see the exemption flow above) or a registry/network failure. Nothing is left half-installed to clean up.

Temporary Authenticated DSH Web README · Troubleshooting：**A restart invalidated the URL.** Only the port is reused, and only when it is free; the launch token changes on every start and restart, so older links answer 401. Call `dsh_web_status` for the current `url`.

**`dsh_web_stop` reports nothing was stopped.** This session had no instance by then — already stopped, killed from the task roster, or ended with `job_kill`. `dsh_web_status` confirms before you assume it failed.
